text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's parliament approved a $40 million loan agreement with the World Bank to fund critical imports of medicines and grains. Under the agreement which was signed last week Bulgaria has to repay the loan in 20 years with five years grace period.

-- Some 86 percent of the Bulgarians have lived below the poverty minimum last year, Bulgaria's biggest Confederation of Independent Trade Unions said. In 1992 the poor Bulgarians were estimated at 21 percent.
-- Bulgaria's state owned Hebros bank's board has agreed to extend credits worth some 25 billion levs to fund grain purchasing from this year's crop, bank's executive director Kostadin Iliev said.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected to discuss today a regulations to issue licenses to commodity exchanges and wholesale markets, Trade ministry officials said.
Under the project the license fee for a commodity exchange is set at five million levs and wholesale market license fee is set at three million levs.
-- Bulgaria's soccer club Levski Sofia has paid $500,000, the highest local transfer fee so far for Lokomotiv Plovdiv's striker Georgi Ivanov, the newspaper said without quoting sources.

-- Bulgaria has proposed a bilateral agreement to Macedonia to ease customs duties, a Bulgarian senior customs official said. Under the draft agreement customs fees on commodities traded between the two Balkan countries will be set at one percent.

-- Germany's Heidelberger Zement AG has bought 51 percent of Bulgaria's Zlatna Panega cement plant and 75 percent of Granatoid plant for a total of $27.5 million, deputy Prime minister Evgeni Bakardzhiev said.
-- Bulgaria's parliament approved new amendments to the Insurance law uder which foreign insurance companies are allowed to set up branches in the country.

-- European Bank for Reconstruction and Development's board has approved buying a 35 percent stake in the Bulgarian state United Bulgarian Bank, Bulgarian Bank Consolidation Company said. The deal is expected to be finalised by Tuesday. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
